summary: Corrected integration verification failure: the prior run's diff-bounded change-set command was staging-state-dependent — it asserted `git diff --name-only` (worktree vs index) equals {src/app.rs, src/app/root.rs, src/ui/layout.rs} and untracked equals {src/app/spawn.rs}. In the integrated worktree the entire change set is staged in the index (5 entries, index vs HEAD at 990112d), so `git diff --name-only` returned empty and `diff` emitted `0a1,3` with nonzero exit, failing verification on the very check meant to protect the diff bound. The implementation itself survived integration untouched: `git diff --cached` is purely additive (575 insertions, 0 deletions across the 5 intended files; no conflict markers) despite upstream ead188a..HEAD heavily modifying the same two files (src/app/root.rs +209, src/ui/layout.rs +80 for the feature-approval workflow); every ticket element sits at its designed anchor (OpenWorkspace enum variant and the exact-label 'Open workspace' menu row immediately before the Disconnect row; `pub mod spawn;`; spawn.rs with resolve_self_executable/spawn_sibling + 4 unit tests; spawn_target_override field/None default; open_workspace handler adjacent to disconnect; the HeaderAction::OpenWorkspace match arm; two board_tests UI tests). The replacement check computes the change set vs HEAD in a staging-independent way ({ git diff --name-only HEAD; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | sort -u) and demands exactly the 5 intended paths. Fresh post-integration gate evidence on pinned rustc/cargo 1.98.1: full `cargo test` rc=0 (409 passed, 0 failed, 1 opt-in ignored), `cargo test --lib app::spawn` 4/4, `--lib open_workspace` 2/2, `--lib chat_store` 2/2; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock byte-identical to HEAD; no `env_clear` outside comments in spawn.rs; src/main.rs still arg-blind; and clippy --all-targets parity versus a fresh shadow expansion of the rebased pre-work base (112==112 sorted '^warning' lines, empty diff, zero warnings naming spawn_sibling/resolve_self_executable/OpenWorkspace/spawn_target_override). Residual caveat, unchanged: the pixel-level two-window demonstration needs a display server, absent in this headless container; every mechanism feeding it (arg-blind zero-args spawn, Wholesale env inheritance, Welcome-default screen, zero-side-effect handler, failure+retry path) is automation-proved.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a connected window mid-way through a planner turn (status line reads '● Working'), when the operator opens Workspace and clicks 'Open workspace', then a second Packet window appears presenting the initial screen (path field, Open button) within a couple of seconds, and the first window's turn keeps advancing with no 'Turn aborted' toast and no change to its draft or status.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Re-verified on the integrated base (HEAD 990112d, change set staged): `cargo test --lib open_workspace` (2 passed, 0 failed) drives the real Workspace menu click into 'Open workspace' with a genuinely hanging turn and asserts the 'Opening a new Packet window' toast paints, no 'Turn aborted' text appears, screen stays Connected, and the turn keeps its registered controller. Initial-screen landing is proven mechanically: src/main.rs inspects no argv (gate command greps `env::args` and fails loudly if present — rc=0 in this run), spawn_sibling launches `Command::new(bin)` with zero arguments, `PacketApp::default()` initializes `screen: Screen::Welcome`, and the env-inheritance unit test proves the sibling sees the parent's whole environment. Limitation stated plainly: this headless container has no display server, so two simultaneous native windows remain the manual mile, exercisable per the runbook (mid-turn on a display host, Workspace > 'Open workspace', second window parks on Welcome while the first keeps '● Working'; kill either, the other survives).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the same connected window, when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then the invoking window's active turn, active implementations, queue and draft are unchanged in state (observably: no cancel requests issued, screen still Connected, composer draft text identical), because the new handler touches none of those fields.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Re-run and green on the integrated base: `open_workspace_spawns_a_detached_sibling_without_touching_the_session` presets a fake in-flight state (live TurnController backed by a harness that hangs until canceled, an idle Controller in active_implementations, an unsent composer draft), performs two consecutive menu clicks, and after each asserts Arc::ptr_eq of the still-registered active turn, `cancel_requested() == false` on the turn, `cancellation_requested() == false` on the active implementation, `chat_draft()` byte-identical, and `matches!(screen, Connected)`. The handler (`PacketApp::open_workspace`, src/app/root.rs:1290) touches only `toasts` and performs the spawn — no request_cancel, no screen/dialog/synth/queue mutation — and the upstream refactor landed around it without altering the contract (match arm at root.rs:2015, staged purely-additive diff confirms zero deletions).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an environment started with PACKET_HOME=<scratch-dir> and PACKET_PI_BIN=<custom path>, when 'Open workspace' spawns a sibling, then the sibling reads the same overridden home and harness binary (observable: its session state lands under <scratch-dir> and its harness discovery probes the custom binary), because the spawn copies no environment deliberately — it inherits wholesale.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Green on the integrated base: `app::spawn::tests::spawn_sibling_inherits_the_parent_environment_wholesale` spawns a probe script THROUGH spawn_sibling; the child records its observed $HOME to a fresh file and the test asserts the round-tripped value equals the parent's exactly — variables the launching process already holds (the same slots PACKET_HOME, PACKET_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECS and PACKET_PI_BIN occupy) travel intact because the spawn clears nothing. Complementary static gate: the comment-stripping grep for `env_clear` over src/app/spawn.rs exits nonzero-if-found and passed (INHERITANCE_AND_ARGBLIND_INVARIANTS_HOLD) in the exact-command reruns; all four spawn unit tests pass (`cargo test --lib app::spawn`, 4/4).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the spawn fails (simulated in tests by pointing the seam at a nonexistent binary; in practice a deleted/moved executable), when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then a warning toast appears embedding the failing binary path or IO error, the menu closed cleanly, the screen stays Connected, and no partially-started zombie interaction occurs; clicking again retries identically.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Green on the integrated base: `open_workspace_spawn_failure_warns_with_path_and_leaves_the_session_usable` points the test seam at a nonexistent binary, clicks 'Open workspace', and asserts the warning paints the failing-path token, no success toast fired, screen remains Connected, draft intact; a SECOND click then repeats the identical graceful failure (repeat-request stability, no zombie half-interaction). Module level: `spawn_sibling_missing_binary_reports_failure_with_the_path_embedded` asserts the Err embeds '/nonexistent/packet-sibling-bin' and returns in far under 2 s (suite green, no panic/hang). Menu closure is the shared `s.on_header_action(action); ui.close();` loop in src/ui/layout.rs that every sibling entry uses.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given two sibling windows both connected to the SAME repository, when both persist chat or contended for the implementation queue, then no corrupt interleaved file bytes appear (atomic rename-swap writes win whole) and queue access serializes through the existing filesystem lock — no crash, no lost-update corruption beyond last-whole-write-wins.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: This ticket introduces no cross-process state or new locking — the sibling is a separate OS process, and the re-run containment gate proves the integrated change set is exactly the 5 intended paths ({git diff --name-only HEAD; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard;} | sort -u), so the two same-repo defenses remain the PRE-EXISTING primitives, byte-untouched and green in this run: per-slug chat persistence writes exclusively through crate::artifacts::atomic_write (rename-swap; `cargo test --lib chat_store` 2/2, including torn_trailing_line_is_skipped_not_fatal) and implementation-queue contention serializes through implementation_queue::acquire's inter-process flock (stock error text: 'Auto queue is already running in another Packet window'). Last-whole-write-wins is the established NFR-2 semantic; no weaker path is introduced by this diff (purely additive, 0 deletions).

S="$(mktemp -d /tmp/chg003-hb.XXXXXX)"
